name: roadmap_query
description: READ-ONLY. The PRECISE tool for Roadmap-card questions — always prefer this over notion_search for anything about cards on the Roadmap board: card status ('what's WIP / under review'), a specific card's Design Status, who's on a card, finding a card from a vague or partial title, or a card number. Queries the live Roadmap database directly: title, link, card number, Design Status, Dev Status, pillars, and people per card. Title and card-number lookups are matched by the SERVER across the whole board, so a card is found wherever it sits — but ALWAYS believe the `note` in the result over any assumption of completeness: on a large unfiltered read it may report a PARTIAL set, and a miss on a partial read means 'I couldn't find it', never 'it doesn't exist'. Title lookups return ranked fuzzy candidates — when a user describes a card vaguely, use these to suggest the closest matches with links ('did you mean…') instead of asking for a link. A named thing that isn't a card may be a doc — check notion_search before concluding it doesn't exist. Combine filters freely (e.g. design_status + person). Safe to call freely (read-only, no gate).

design_status.description: Filter by exact Design Status column value, e.g. 'WIP', 'Under Review', 'Ready for Design', 'Under Dev', 'Shipped'. If the value is wrong, the error lists the valid options — retry with one.

title.description: Full, partial, or vague card title/description — fuzzy-matched against every card on the board; returns ranked candidates.

person.description: A person's name (or part of it) — matches cards where they appear in any people column (Contributor, Dev, …).

card_number.description: The card's numeric id as shown on the board (e.g. 2436).

name: notion_search
description: READ-ONLY. Search Notion for pages and database entries by keyword when you do NOT already have a URL. Prefer a narrow `scope` when you know the surface — scoped queries hit the live database directly (full-database read + fuzzy title match) and beat workspace search. Believe the result's `note` over any assumption of completeness: a large catalog can exceed what one call reads, and a miss on such a read means 'I couldn't find it', never 'it doesn't exist'. Scopes: 'team' (SME roster), 'apps' (access-request routing — Application Admin grants; you only route), 'marketplace' (prototype catalog), 'help_tutors' / 'help_teachers' (Help Center articles), 'decisions' (Decisions DB), 'running_notes' (Design Running Notes), 'news' / 'success_stories' / 'research_papers' / 'banners' (Content HQ read radar), 'any' (workspace title search — last resort). NOT for Roadmap cards — use roadmap_query. Returns titles + URLs (+ key properties); follow up with source_read for full content. Only pages the uno-bot integration is connected to are searchable; if nothing comes back, say so rather than guessing. Docs may be stale or ASPIRATIONAL (roadmap PRDs, future specs): check the linked card's Design/Dev Status and decision state before stating a doc's content as current fact — for how-it-works-today questions the blueprint is primary, and a doc-vs-blueprint conflict is surfaced, never blended. Safe to call freely (read-only, no gate).

query.description: What to find, in plain words, e.g. 'PRD for tutor matching', 'onboarding decision', 'high-fi toolkit prototypes', 'session count help article'.

scope.description: 'team' = Team Member roster. 'apps' = Third Party Applications (access routing). 'marketplace' = Prototype Marketplace. 'help_tutors' / 'help_teachers' = Help Center article DBs. 'decisions' = Decisions DB. 'running_notes' = Design Running Notes. 'news' / 'success_stories' / 'research_papers' / 'banners' = Content HQ. 'any' = workspace-wide title search (prefer a catalog scope when you know the surface). Card lookups → roadmap_query.

name: source_read
description: READ-ONLY. Fetch the actual CONTENT of a link before answering — a Notion page (returns title + properties incl. Owner/people + block text), a Figma frame (returns node name/type + text layers), a GitHub/raw file, or any web URL (returns text). Use this WHENEVER the request contains or references a URL, a linked PRD/doc/guide, or a Figma frame: read it and ground your answer in the returned content, then cite it. Never answer a question about a linked source from memory/priors. For 'who owns/should review this' questions, read the page and use its Owner/people property rather than guessing. Safe to call freely (read-only, no gate).

url.description: The full http(s) URL to read (Notion, Figma, GitHub, or any web page).

name: search_blueprint
description: READ-ONLY. Query the uno-blueprint (Supabase — the source of truth for the CURRENT service journey: who does what, at which scenario/path/step, per layer actor). Use this FIRST for any how-does-it-work-today question and ALWAYS cite the row(s). Most rows describe current state, but the board ALSO carries a labelled future layer, marked by the PATH NAME: `Planned: <topic>` = decided and scheduled, not yet shipped; `Prototype: <topic>` = exploratory, may never ship. Report the first as 'is changing', the second as 'might change', and neither as how it works today. Roadmap cards + PRDs remain primary for what's planned; blueprint rows are the today-baseline for explaining the delta. NEVER assert the blueprint has no future state for a scenario until you have searched THAT scenario for a `Planned:` or `Prototype:` path. When a Notion doc conflicts with a blueprint row, surface the conflict, never blend: a WIP/under-review card = planned change (say 'is changing' only if decided, 'might change' if exploratory); a shipped card that disagrees = the doc is likely obsolete (paired writes update the blueprint at ship) — keep the blueprint answer, and if the blueprint itself seems stale say so and offer a maintenance intake. No rows → that is a fact about the QUERY, not about the blueprint: check `index` or re-search under the scenario's own name before saying the blueprint has nothing; a CURRENT doc (Help Center, shipped PRD) may then answer, cited and dated — never fabricate. Rows carry `url` (a deep link that opens THAT cell in the blueprint app — link the cells you rely on, verbatim, never hand-built), may carry `links` (URLs the blueprint authors attached — authored, safe to surface) and `updatedAt` (use it to judge staleness instead of assuming currency). Each row also carries `matchedBy` — which retrievers found it: `vector` (semantic similarity alone), `keyword` (the cell's own prose), `structural` (its phase/scenario/path/step/layer name), or a `+`-joined combination. USE IT FOR CONFIDENCE: a row several retrievers agree on matched the blueprint's own words; a `vector`-only row is a semantic guess and deserves a hedge. If EVERY row is `vector`-only, nothing in the blueprint actually mentions your terms — treat that as evidence the topic may be absent, and never present such a row as the answer. Similarity score cannot tell you this: answer-less questions score in the same range as real hits, so corroboration is the signal and `score` is not. The result reports `retrieval` (`hybrid` = the current fused path, all retrievers ran; `semantic`/`rpc`/`tables` = legacy fallbacks, only if the fused path was unavailable), `truncated` + `capped_by` (semantic | max_rows — when truncated, say the list is partial), `cached` + `age_ms` (true = these rows were NOT read this turn, so claim no freshness), and `thin` (legacy fallback only — the fused path never sets it). When `orientation` is `live`, `index` is the COMPLETE list of phases → scenarios → paths, read this turn: name the phase from it, quote counts only from its own `scale`, and settle the NEVER-rule above against its `[Planned]`/`[Prototype]` markers; `unavailable` means you could not check, so claim no absence. Ask for it any time with `include: ["index"]`. Follow the `notes` array — each entry is one obligation that applies to THIS result. Safe to call freely (read-only, no gate).

query.description: Free-text query describing what you need from the blueprint, e.g. 'Tutor Admin redesign status', 'decisions about empty states'.

include.description: Optional extra reads, ONE SUBREQUEST EACH — ask only for what the question needs. 'edges': cells one hop from the matches (what they trigger / are triggered by) for "what breaks if we change X". 'findings': audit issues already recorded against these cells. 'slices': named views someone already cut, to point at instead of improvising one. Omit for ordinary how-does-it-work questions.

name: github_read
description: READ-ONLY. Read from the plus-uno GitHub repo — fetch a file's contents by repo-relative path (DS agent-views, rule docs, AGENTS.md, a component's source), or list a directory to check what EXISTS (a directory path returns its entries automatically). Use it to confirm a design-system component before proposing component_implement (read `design-system/src/components`), or to ground a review in the actual rule docs rather than memory. For an arbitrary GitHub URL a designer pasted, prefer source_read; use github_read when you know the path or need a directory listing. Safe to call freely (read-only, no gate).

ref.description: Optional git ref (branch/tag/sha). Defaults to the repo's default branch.

search.description: Code-search mode: find WHERE something lives in the repo (e.g. 'focus-ring', 'PageLayout') — returns matching file paths + github.com links to read or cite. When set, 'path' is ignored.

name: slack_user_profile
description: READ-ONLY. Look up a Slack user's profile by id — display name, title/role, email, timezone, status. Use when you need to know WHO someone is (a member id from slack_channel_members, an @-mention in the thread, a card contributor's Slack identity). Mention people as <@id> in replies. Safe to call freely (read-only, no gate).

user_id.description: Slack user id (U…), bare or as an <@U…> mention.

name: slack_channel_members
description: READ-ONLY. List a Slack channel's member ids (first 100) — for 'who's in #plus-design', review-routing, or checking whether someone is in a channel before referring them there. The bot must be in the channel. Returns ids; mention them as <@id> (Slack renders names), and use slack_user_profile for a specific person's role — don't fetch every profile. Safe to call freely (read-only, no gate).

channel_id.description: Slack channel id (C…), bare or as a <#C…> mention.

name: slack_thread_read
description: READ-ONLY. Read the messages of a Slack thread you were given a link to (outside this conversation's own memory) — to tally handoff sign-offs (dev/PM/stakeholder ✅), read reviewer verdicts, or pull a source discussion to synthesize into findings. Pass the Slack message/thread permalink. The bot must be a member of the channel. Safe to call freely (read-only, no gate).

link.description: A Slack message or thread permalink, e.g. 'https://plus-team.slack.com/archives/C03FC8AS69K/p1720000000000000'.

name: slack_react
description: Add an emoji reaction AS UNO-BOT to a message in the current thread. Use freely to acknowledge, celebrate, or signal state — any workspace emoji name (without colons), e.g. 'tada', 'eyes', 'raised_hands', or a custom workspace emoji. Reactions are reversible and ungated. For a PURE acknowledgement from the user ('thanks', 'got it', 'nice') react and end your turn with NO text — the reaction is the whole reply. Refused for the gate emoji (white_check_mark, heavy_check_mark, +1, thumbsup, no_entry, x, negative_squared_cross_mark, no_entry_sign): those resolve proposal cards. If message_ts is omitted, reacts to the user's current message.

emoji.description: Emoji name without colons, e.g. 'tada' or 'rocket'.

message_ts.description: Optional Slack ts of the message to react to (must be in the current channel). Defaults to the user's current message.

name: slack_search
description: READ-ONLY. Search Slack messages. Results arrive PRE-CLEARED by a Worker-side visibility firewall — safe to quote as returned. Three modes (see result.visibility): 'public-only' (no user credential stored — public channels are the entire search), 'workspace-filtered' (public + team-allowlisted private channels; DMs never included), and 'requester-own' (active only when the requester has connected their Slack history AND is asking in their own DM with you — results then include their DMs, group DMs, and private channels, i.e. exactly what they can already see). Requester-own results answer that requester in that DM only — never repeat DM-derived content anywhere else. `searched_surfaces` says what was actually looked at. An empty result means nothing matched THERE — scope the absence IN THE SAME SENTENCE as the finding ("nothing in the public channels I can see"), never a bare "no one has mentioned this"; when the result carries `absence_scope`, follow it exactly. `withheld_private_matches` appears ONLY in the requester's own DM, where saying "there were matches I can't surface" is safe; it is absent elsewhere BY DESIGN, because the count alone tells a room that private material exists on the topic — never infer or mention withheld hits when the field is not there. If the result carries a `note` with a connect link, offer it when the requester wanted wider coverage.

query.description: Slack search query. Supports operators like in:#channel, from:@user, before:/after: dates.

name: notion_create
description: Create a new page or card — SIDE EFFECT, routed through the confirmation gate. `surface` selects WHERE and WHAT is created: 'prd' (design PRD on the Roadmap board), 'intake' (maintenance intake on the Roadmap board), or 'decision' (Decisions DB row under Design HQ — requires properties.roadmap_card). Research docs and marketplace entries are NOT bot surfaces — they run in-IDE. Draft the content conversationally first and let the designer refine it; only invoke once they approve. Follow docs/conventions/notion.md for required properties and body shape — NEVER create select options / pillars / OKRs; exact-match existing option names. Keep content grounded in the conversation; put genuine unknowns under an 'Open Questions' section rather than inventing.

surface.description: Where to file it: 'prd' (feature or DS-component PRD card on the Roadmap board), 'intake' (maintenance/request intake card, Product Pillar: Universal + Product Tag: Maintenance), or 'decision' (Decisions DB row — requires properties.roadmap_card; optional Status/Evidence). Research docs and marketplace entries are created in-IDE, not by the bot.

summary.description: 1-3 sentence overview, rendered as the opening of the body. Markdown renders: **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code```, --- dividers, and - [ ] checkboxes. Headings inside a body render one level below the section heading. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

sections.description: Body sections in order (Problem/Context, Goals, Users & Scenarios, Requirements, Open Questions, etc.). Markdown renders: **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code```, --- dividers, and - [ ] checkboxes. Headings inside a body render one level below the section heading. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

body.description: Section body. Markdown renders: **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code```, --- dividers, and - [ ] checkboxes. Headings inside a body render one level below the section heading. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

acceptance_criteria.description: For 'prd'/'prd' (component PRDs included): checklist rendered as Notion to-do checkboxes (read downstream by component_implement / prototype_scaffold). Inline Markdown renders: **bold**, `code`, [label](url).

properties.description: Surface-specific card properties as key→value, exact-matched against the live schema by the tool (PRD: product_pillar; intake: evidence_link, suggested_tier; decision: roadmap_card [required], status, evidence). Only include what the conversation supports; never invent option names.

source_url.description: Optional link back to the source — a Slack permalink to the discussion, or a Figma link.

name: notion_update
description: Update an existing Notion page/card — SIDE EFFECT, routed through the confirmation gate. Works on ANY page or database the bot is shared on (not just the Roadmap board): Roadmap cards, Decisions DB rows, per-person running-notes pages, any DB. Two uses, combinable: (1) change PROPERTIES via `properties` — the tool reads the page's live database schema and matches your property name to it case/space/underscore-insensitively, then writes by the REAL type, so "Dev Status", "Dev_Status", a Date, a Person, a URL, a number, a checkbox all work. It NEVER invents a select/status option — if a value isn't an existing option it reports back instead of guessing (Notion auto-creates on mismatch). (2) append narrative blocks via `append` — append, never overwrite a human-owned body. Pass the page URL.

page_url.description: The Notion URL (or page id) of the card/page to update.

properties.description: Property changes as name→value (string values). The tool matches each name to the page's live database schema (case/space/underscore-insensitive) and formats by the real Notion type — status, select, multi_select (comma-separated), date (ISO, or "start → end"), number, checkbox, url, email, rich text, title. select/status/multi_select values must be EXISTING options (unknown ones are reported, never created). People/relation need a Notion id or URL.

append.description: Narrative blocks to append to the end of the page body. Markdown renders: **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code```, --- dividers, and - [ ] checkboxes. Headings inside a body render one level below the section heading. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

sections.description: Headed sections to append. Markdown renders: **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code```, --- dividers, and - [ ] checkboxes. Headings inside a body render one level below the section heading. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

text.description: A single block of text to append (use when no heading is needed, e.g. a dated progress pulse). Markdown renders: **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code```, --- dividers, and - [ ] checkboxes. Headings inside a body render one level below the section heading. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

name: notion_archive
description: Archive (soft-delete) a Notion page/card — SIDE EFFECT, routed through the confirmation gate. Use to undo or remove a page the designer asks to delete ('delete that', 'remove that card', 'undo'). Works on any page the bot can reach, not just cards it created. Archiving moves the page to Notion's trash (recoverable); the ✅ confirmation gate + requester identity are the safety. Pass the page URL (typically the link the bot posted when it created the card).

page_url.description: The Notion URL (or page id) of the card to archive.

name: component_implement
description: Open a draft PR that implements a named design-system component change, by triggering the figma-implement GitHub Action — SIDE EFFECT, routed through the confirmation gate. Use ONLY when the designer clearly asks for a specific named component (e.g. 'implement Badge', 'go ahead with the Badge change'). REQUIRES a Notion PRD: the polling bot creates one and posts it in #uno-bot. If the thread already has that PRD notification, proceed (the Worker reads it from the thread); if there is NO PRD, do NOT invoke — ask for the PRD link first, then pass notion_prd_url. Confirm the component exists first with github_read (list design-system/src/components) if unsure. Never invent the component name or PRD URL. For a NEW prototype from a Figma frame, use prototype_scaffold instead.

component.description: The component name as it appears in the Figma library, exact casing (e.g. 'Badge', 'Button', 'CardSurface').

notion_prd_url.description: The Notion PRD link for this change. Usually read automatically from the polling-bot notification in the thread — only set this when the designer pastes a PRD link themselves.

notes.description: Optional free-form implementation notes from the designer. Pass through verbatim if present; omit otherwise.

name: prototype_scaffold
description: Scaffold a NEW prototypes prototype from a Figma design (page/screen/flow), by triggering the figma-implement-design GitHub Action to open a draft PR — SIDE EFFECT, routed through the confirmation gate. Use when the designer pastes a Figma URL and asks for a prototype (e.g. 'scaffold a prototypes for this frame', 'build this design <figma.com/...>'). A Notion PRD link is OPTIONAL but preferred — ask if they have one for better context; if not, offer to build straight from the frame and, on their OK, invoke with notion_prd_url omitted. Never invent a PRD URL. Do NOT use for named DS-library component work — that is component_implement.

figma_url.description: Full Figma URL the designer pasted, e.g. 'https://www.figma.com/design/NUcRDZUzUiuVmx1ydNXpl3/APPLICATION-PROTOTYPES?node-id=158-21725'. Must contain a node-id query param.

notion_prd_url.description: Optional. Full notion.so URL of a PRD for this prototype, if the designer has one. Never invent it; omit if they choose to skip.

slug.description: Optional kebab-case folder name for prototypes/{slug}/. Must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,40}$. If omitted, derived from the Figma node name.

notes.description: Optional free-form implementation notes from the designer. Pass through verbatim.

name: shareout_post
description: Share a prototype/design/PRD with the team FOR FEEDBACK (the 'publish' / 'share out' / 'post for feedback' action). Posts a shareout to #plus-design-feedback: what it is, a link back, a feedback prompt, and @-mentioned reviewers — SIDE EFFECT (it pings people), routed through the confirmation gate. This is NOT marketplace registration: use this when the designer wants eyes/critique/feedback — catalog registration runs in-IDE via writers/notion, not through any bot tool. Stage IMMEDIATELY with whatever links are in hand — do NOT interrogate for missing bundle pieces first; the confirmation card automatically flags anything missing (Loom / live preview / Decisions link) and the user's ✅ is informed consent to post without them (policy 2026-07-16).

summary.description: One or two sentences: what is being shared and what feedback is wanted.

link.description: Link to the artifact (prototype URL, Figma frame, PR, or PRD).

reviewers.description: Reviewers to tag — Slack user IDs (U…) ONLY, never display names (a plain name renders as dead text and pings nobody). Resolve IDs via notion_search(scope:'team') slackUserId or the PRD Owner before invoking; if you can't resolve an ID, leave the person out and say so in the preview.

deadline.description: Optional human-readable feedback deadline, e.g. 'EOD Friday'.

name: email_send
description: Send an email via Gmail on the design team's behalf — SIDE EFFECT (sends a real email), routed through the confirmation gate. Use for outward notifications a Slack message can't cover: emailing an external SME/collaborator, sending a PRD or prototype summary to a stakeholder, or a follow-up the designer explicitly asks to send by email. Draft the email conversationally first (recipient, subject, body) and let the designer refine it; only invoke once they approve. Never invent recipient addresses — ask for them if unknown. Prefer Slack for anything that can stay in Slack.

to.description: Recipient email address(es). Never invent — use addresses the designer provided.

body.description: Plain-text email body. Write it out fully — no placeholders.

name: proposal_resolve
description: Resolve a side-effect proposal that is awaiting user confirmation. Use when the system prompt shows a pending proposal AND the user's current message is a decision about it, in whatever words — a yes ('go ahead', 'sure', 'ok', 'sounds good', 'yep do it') confirms; a no ('cancel', 'no', 'scrap it') cancels. Anyone in the thread may confirm or cancel — not just the original requester. If the message asks for a change, or asks something unrelated, do NOT invoke — reply conversationally and the proposal sits until someone presses ✅ / ⛔ on the card, reacts, or it expires after 60 minutes.

decision.description: 'confirm' to proceed with the proposed action as-is. 'cancel' to stop or change direction (for a parameter change, cancel then stage a fresh proposal).

message_to_user.description: Short Slack mrkdwn message to post alongside the resolution, e.g. 'Got it — firing the implement for Badge now.' Keep to one or two sentences.
